# Review pack: Haman

**Status: DRAFT, unreviewed, unpublished.** Generated from `content/stories/haman.draft.json`; do not edit this file (regenerate it).

Quran text: Tanzil Project (https://tanzil.net/), Uthmani 1.1, CC BY 3.0, reproduced verbatim. The English is the drafter's own wording of what the ayat state; it is not a translation of the Quran.

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Haman is described as Fir'awn's minister or vizier, and later works discuss his origin and his end.
- Whether Haman is a personal name or a title is not settled by the text.
- Hadith to add later: reports about Haman, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. Named with Fir'awn  (`#named-with-firawn`)

Cited ayat: 28:6, 28:8

> **28:6** وَنُمَكِّنَ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَنُرِىَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا مِنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَحْذَرُونَ

> **28:8** فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ

### Claims

**c1** (28:6): God wished to show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces, through those who were weakened, what they feared.

**c2** (28:8): The family of Fir'awn picked up the child, so that he would become an enemy and a source of grief to them, and Fir'awn, Haman and their forces were in error.

### One-minute summary

God wished to show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces what they feared [c1]. The ayah names Haman among those who were in error when the family of Fir'awn picked up the child [c2].

### Complete story

God wished to show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces, through those who were weakened, what they feared [c1]. The family of Fir'awn picked up the child, so that he would become an enemy and a source of grief to them, and Fir'awn, Haman and their forces were in error [c2].

### Deep study

In both ayat Haman is named after Fir'awn and before the forces [c1][c2]. The ayat do not give his office, and they do not say what he did [c1].

### Kids mode

The Quran names Haman beside Fir'awn and their forces [c1][c2]. God wished to show them what they feared [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the Quran names Haman among those who were in error [c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: Haman's office, his origin or his time.
- Not established: what Haman did in these events.
- Not established: what they feared, beyond the words of the ayah.

## 2. Told to build  (`#told-to-build`)

Cited ayat: 28:38, 40:36-37

> **28:38** وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلْمَلَأُ مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى فَأَوْقِدْ لِى يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ عَلَى ٱلطِّينِ فَٱجْعَل لِّى صَرْحًا لَّعَلِّىٓ أَطَّلِعُ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّهُۥ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰذِبِينَ

> **40:36** وَقَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ يَٰهَٰمَٰنُ ٱبْنِ لِى صَرْحًا لَّعَلِّىٓ أَبْلُغُ ٱلْأَسْبَٰبَ
>
> **40:37** أَسْبَٰبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ فَأَطَّلِعَ إِلَىٰٓ إِلَٰهِ مُوسَىٰ وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّهُۥ كَٰذِبًا وَكَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِفِرْعَوْنَ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ وَصُدَّ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمَا كَيْدُ فِرْعَوْنَ إِلَّا فِى تَبَابٍ

### Claims

**c1** (28:38): Fir'awn told Haman to light a fire on clay and make him a lofty tower, so that he might climb up to the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar.

**c2** (40:36-37): Fir'awn told Haman to build him a tower so that he might reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, and look at the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar.

### One-minute summary

Fir'awn told Haman to build him a lofty tower so that he might climb up to the god of Musa [c1][c2]. He said that he thought Musa a liar [c1].

### Complete story

Fir'awn told Haman to light a fire on clay and make him a lofty tower, so that he might climb up to the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar [c1]. Fir'awn told Haman to build him a tower so that he might reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, and look at the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar [c2].

### Deep study

One passage tells Haman to light a fire on clay and the other to build [c1][c2]. Neither says whether Haman did it or whether the tower was finished [c2].

### Kids mode

Fir'awn told Haman to build him a lofty tower [c1]. He wanted to climb up to the god of Musa [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passages record an order given to Haman and not his answer [c1][c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: whether Haman built the tower, or how he answered.
- Not established: what became of Haman.
